findings.description: ADR 0113 changes what decision 53 says: 0053 line 12 claims `core.bigFileThreshold=1` makes every text file `-\t-`, and 0113 pins that away. Neither file links the other. Add `- Amends: [0053](…)` to 0113 and `- Amended by: [0113](…)` to 0053, following the 0076/0074 header practice described in ADR 0109.

The new GIT_SAFE_CONFIG and diffHunks comments spell out the whole mechanism (`-\t-` → forged; patience/histogram reading a block as deleted and re-added). ADR 113 and the test comments say the same thing. A one-line WHY plus `(decision 113)` would do (AGENTS.md §Comments).

The new interHunkContext, diff-algorithm, copies-numstat and `:(top)foo` tests each inline the makeRepo/commit/checkout -b feature/commit scaffold. The `repoWith(base, feature)` helper already does this, but it is scoped inside the gitDiffBinaryRecount describe. Moving it to module scope would remove the repetition.

The index entry and title for 0113 have no trailing period after the date, while 0107 and 0111 end in `(2026-10-27).`. The index is already inconsistent (0109 also has none), so ignore this if the generator decides.

On macOS, a session-written `core.precomposeUnicode=true` (it lives in the shared common-dir config) rewrites diffHunks' NFD path argument to NFC. `--literal-pathspecs` does not stop this, so a file committed under an NFD name returns no hunks and drops out of patch coverage. Pinning `-c core.precomposeUnicode=false` on this call would close it. Darwin only; not reproduced on Linux.
